name: PCA territory, occipital
summary: The occipital PCA territory is the medial and inferior occipital lobe supplied by the calcarine and parieto-occipital arteries, the terminal branches of the posterior cerebral artery: the calcarine cortex, the cuneus, the lingual gyrus, the occipital fusiform gyrus and the medial occipital pole. It is the territory of the homonymous hemianopia, congruous and often macular-sparing, and of the visual agnosias, achromatopsia and alexia that follow ventral occipital infarction; bilateral infarction produces cortical blindness. It is supplied through a single P2-P3 trunk that embolism from the vertebrobasilar system or the heart blocks, and its cortex is exposed to the posterior watershed on its lateral edge.

anatomy.location: Medial occipital surface (cuneus, calcarine cortex, lingual gyrus) and the inferior occipital surface (occipital fusiform gyrus), the medial part of the occipital pole and the parieto-occipital sulcus region, with the underlying white matter of the optic radiation's posterior part and the forceps major; bounded laterally by the MCA occipital territory and in front by the temporal PCA territory and the ACA territory at the precuneus.

efferents.to: Internal occipital veins to the great cerebral vein and the transverse sinus

function: The territory contains the primary visual cortex and the ventral extrastriate areas of color, form and reading, so its infarction produces a contralateral hemianopia or quadrantanopia (depending on which calcarine bank is involved), hemiachromatopsia, and, in the dominant hemisphere with the splenium, alexia without agraphia; the occipital pole receives collateral MCA supply and survives in many occlusions, and leptomeningeal anastomoses with the MCA along the lateral occipital surface determine the size of the infarct. It is also the region affected in posterior reversible encephalopathy, migraine aura and occipital epilepsy, all of which mimic transient ischemia.

bestView.label: occipital PCA territory on the medial occipital lobe

imaging.normalAppearance: On the overlay the occipital PCA domain covers the medial and inferior occipital lobe; the calcarine sulcus lies at its center and the pole at its posterior edge.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion of the medial occipital cortex with a congruous homonymous hemianopia, macula spared when the pole is MCA-supplied.
Bilateral calcarine restricted diffusion with cortical blindness and Anton denial.
Normal diffusion during a scintillating scotoma; transient perfusion asymmetry only.

examination: Reading and color naming by hemifield
Pupillary reactions, normal in cortical visual loss
pearls: A congruous hemianopia with normal pupils is occipital
The occipital PCA territory is embolic territory: find the source
Migraine, PRES, seizure and stroke all live in the occipital lobe; time course and DWI separate them
